theme.image_style: documentary photograph, archival, no AI illustration
theme.visual_style: Narrative History: archival history embedded inside an open book page frame; warm amber accents; clean data slides

scenes.beat: Establishes the ancient origins of baby walkers through historical evidence
scenes.narration: 西元一千四百四十年，荷蘭一本華麗的彩飾手抄本上，畫著嬰兒耶穌——站在一台四輪木製學步車裡。

visual.alt: Jesus in a baby walker, c. 1440

camera_motion.start_frame: full manuscript image inside the open book page
camera_motion.end_frame: tight focus on the child seated in the four-wheeled walker
camera_motion.direction: gradually pan down and right while zooming in

narration_alt.en: Year 1440. A Dutch illuminated manuscript shows the infant Jesus, sitting in a four-wheeled wooden baby walker.

scenes.beat: Reinforces the historical continuity of walker design across centuries
scenes.narration: 一百多年後，一五八四年。畫家克雷克為薩伏伊王室的小公主畫像，又出現一台一模一樣的學步車。

visual.alt: Maria Apollonia of Savoy, c. 1584

narration_alt.en: A century and a half later, 1584. A court portrait of a Savoy princess shows the exact same design.

scenes.beat: Notes that walker form changed little across nearly six centuries, in neutral hook tone
scenes.narration: 再過三百多年，到一九零五年的照片，依然是同樣的木製框架、同樣的四個輪子。將近六百年，學步車的樣子幾乎沒有改變。

visual.alt: A baby in a sit-in walker, 1905

narration_alt.en: Three centuries later, a 1905 photograph: same seat, same frame, same wheels. Six hundred years unchanged.

scenes.beat: Names the basic parental need the design solves, anchoring its 600-year persistence
scenes.narration: 這個設計能延續六百年，是因為它解決的需求很基本：讓還不會走的嬰兒保持直立、待在視線裡，也讓大人暫時把雙手空出來。

visual.text:
六百年的同一個答案
直立 · 在視線裡 · 空出雙手

narration_alt.en: So why did this design survive six centuries? It solves one basic parental need — keep the not-yet-walking baby upright, in sight, with the adult's hands momentarily free.

scenes.beat: Establishes that for six centuries the device remained a rare aristocratic possession
scenes.narration: 但這個方便，整整六百年都只給少數人。從荷蘭手抄本到薩伏伊宮廷，學步車是木匠的手工作品——一台供一個孩子使用，再傳給下一胎，是貴族家裡才有的稀有財產。

visual.alt: Victorian satirical illustration

narration_alt.en: But for six centuries, that convenience belonged only to a few. From Dutch manuscripts to the Savoy court, the walker was a carpenter's handmade work — one frame per child, passed down to the next, a rare aristocratic possession.

scenes.beat: Frames Sloan's 1901 ad as the first failed attempt at mass-market commercialization
scenes.narration: 一九零一年，第一次有人試著把它變成大眾商品。加拿大旅館老闆湯瑪斯·斯隆，在渥太華日報登了廣告。結果完全沒有市場。一位歷史學家後來這樣總結:「I don't think this idea of a baby-walker took off.」

visual.alt: A baby in a sit-in walker, 1905 — period stand-in for the failed 1901 Sloan commercialization

overlay.name: "I don't think this idea of a baby-walker took off"

narration_alt.en: 1901 — the first time someone tried to make it a mass-market product. Canadian hotelier Thomas Sloan placed an ad in the Ottawa Journal. There was no market. A historian later put it this way:

scenes.beat: Identifies three converging forces—plastic, suburban layouts, women in the workforce—that finally made the walker fit its moment
scenes.narration: 要再等六十年。一九六零、七零年代，三件事同時發生：塑膠射出成型壓低了成本；戰後郊區的開放格局，給了它跑動的空間；女性回到職場，需要一個能放小孩、空出雙手的工具。產品終於對上了時代。

visual.text:
1960–1975 三力合流
塑膠射出成型 → 成本下降
郊區開放格局 → 空間
女性回到職場 → 雙手解放

narration_alt.en: Another sixty years. In the 60s and 70s, three forces converged: cheap plastic injection molding; suburban open-plan homes; and women returning to work, needing somewhere to set the child down. The walker finally fit its moment.

scenes.beat: Period texture for the 1960s–70s boom — boom_era clip narrated as atmosphere only (greenlight term 4)
scenes.narration: 一台塑膠框架、四個輪子，學步車第一次走進尋常人家的客廳。

visual.alt: Generated boom-era period b-roll — atmosphere only, not documentary evidence

scenes.beat: Establishes the 1980s as the cultural peak when walkers became a baby-shower default driven by social trust
scenes.narration: 到了一九八零年代，它變成嬰兒送禮的標配。朋友的寶寶滿月就送一台。理由很簡單：既然每個媽媽都有一台，那就應該沒問題。

visual.alt: Baby in a sit-in walker, San Salvador, August 1972 — the boom era

narration_alt.en: By the 1980s, it became the standard baby-shower gift. A friend's baby reaches one month — you give a walker. The logic was simple: every mother had one, so it must be safe.

scenes.beat: Pivots from market success to medical concern—ER doctors begin seeing a repeating injury pattern
scenes.narration: 但就在每一個育嬰房都擺著一台塑膠框架的同時，醫院急診室的醫師，開始看到一個重複出現的模式。

visual.text:
一個重複
出現的模式

narration_alt.en: But just as every nursery had this plastic frame in it, doctors in hospital emergency rooms began to see a pattern repeating itself.

scenes.beat: 1990 ER-visits peak as animated big number — replaces the static slide
scenes.narration: 一九九零年的數字第一次說清楚：全美急診室那一整年，處理了大約兩萬個跟學步車有關的嬰幼兒受傷。

visual.title: 1990 高峰
visual.background_prompt: aged paper texture, soft sepia stains, faint grid

scenes.beat: Injury pattern as animated bar chart — sequential grow
scenes.narration: 結果，七成四的傷害是從樓梯摔下來，九成一傷在頭或頸部。這不是擦破皮，是顱骨。

visual.title: 受傷的樣態
visual.background_prompt: aged paper texture, soft sepia stains, faint grid

scenes.beat: Emphasizes life-threatening consequences with skull fracture data
scenes.narration: 住院的孩子裡，每三個就有一個顱骨骨折。再小的學步車，撞下樓梯都不是小事。

visual.title: 送醫住院的孩子
visual.background_prompt: aged paper texture, soft sepia stains, faint grid

narration_alt.en: Of children admitted to hospital, more than one in three had skull fractures. A baby on stairs is never a small fall.

scenes.beat: Cumulative 25-year toll as animated big number — replaces the text_card
scenes.narration: 把時間拉長：從一九九零年到二零一四年，整整二十五年，美國有二十三萬零六百七十六個孩子，因為學步車進急診。

visual.title: 二十五年累積
visual.background_prompt: aged paper texture, soft sepia stains, faint grid

scenes.beat: ACT A — speed mechanism + hazard-field framing over the danger_rolling clip
scenes.narration: 一個數字一旦大了，就會麻木。所以想像它怎麼發生：坐入式學步車能讓嬰兒每秒衝出一公尺以上——比同一個房間裡的大人反應還快。

visual.alt: Generated rolling-walker danger clip — motion accent for the speed mechanism

scenes.beat: ACT A — burns hazard endpoint (kettle on stovetop, multi-thousand-px, longer dwell ok)
scenes.narration: 樓梯只是頭條。多出來的那幾公分高度、那幾公尺移動範圍，把整個家變成風險場。爐上一壺滾水——學步車能直接推到爐邊，伸手就搆得到。

visual.alt: Kettle boiling on a gas stove — burn hazard a walker can reach

scenes.beat: ACT A — drowning hazard endpoint
scenes.narration: 還有放滿水的浴缸。對會跑的學步車，那只是一秒鐘的距離。

visual.alt: Claw-foot bathtub, low-angle — drowning hazard a walker can reach

scenes.beat: ACT A — deaths summary as animated stat (1973–1998 + 2004–2008)
scenes.narration: 這些不是假設。有記錄的死亡，一九七三到一九九八年三十四起，二零零四到二零零八年再添八起。

visual.title: 有記錄的死亡
visual.background_prompt: aged paper texture, soft sepia stains, faint grid
visual.subtitle: 1973–1998: 34 起 · 2004–2008: 8 起

scenes.beat: ACT A — poisoning hazard endpoint (drain cleaner; BRIEF beat per greenlight term 2)
scenes.narration: 而且射程還在延伸——原本鎖在高處的強鹼清潔劑，現在也搆得到。燙傷、溺水、中毒——每一種都是有真實病例的機制。

visual.alt: Caustic soda bottles on a floor — poisoning hazard a walker can reach

scenes.beat: ACT B — undercount comparison chart, iceberg reveal (recorded vs estimated-true)
scenes.narration: 而這個二十三萬，幾乎可以確定是低估的。

visual.title: 230,676 只是地板
visual.background_prompt: aged paper texture, soft sepia stains, faint grid
visual.subtitle: NEISS 漏報 + 40+ 種名稱

scenes.beat: ACT B — explain NEISS low sensitivity + 40+ names
scenes.narration: 原因有兩個：一是 CPSC 的 NEISS 傷害資料庫，一九九六年的審計發現它對學步車漏報約百分之四；二是這個產品在學術、新聞、零售貨架上，有超過四十種叫法——名字一亂，就沒人能乾淨地數清楚。真正的數字，只會更高。

visual.text:
真實數字 > 230,676
NEISS 漏報 + 40+ 種名稱

scenes.beat: Lead-in collapsing the 1982 study + voluntary/ASTM standards into one bridge
scenes.narration: 警報其實很早就響了。一九八二年第一篇研究，比一九九零年的高峰還早八年。接下來二十年，標準一條條加上去——問題只有一個：有用嗎？

visual.text:
1982 第一篇研究
二十年 · 標準一條條加上
有用嗎？

scenes.beat: Shows US eventually strengthening regulations with dramatic results
scenes.narration: 有用，而且非常明顯。從一九八二年的研究、一九九五年的自願標準、一九九七年的 ASTM、二零零一年兒科學會、二零零四年加拿大、到二零一零年強制法規——到二零一四年，急診數字只剩兩千出頭，比一九九零年下降了百分之九十。

visual.title: US ER visits per year
visual.background_prompt: aged paper texture, soft sepia stains, faint grid
visual.rationale: trend-over-time data with regulation events as causal markers; the line draws as the narration delivers the 90% verdict, carrying cause-and-effect across the scene

narration_alt.en: 2010, the US finally made standards mandatory. By 2014, ER visits dropped to about 2,000 — ninety percent below the 1990 peak.

scenes.beat: ACT C — Canada total ban: map with BANNED 2004 / STILL SOLD overlay (breaks chart run)
scenes.narration: 二零零四年，有一個國家真的照做了。加拿大成為全世界第一個全面禁止有輪坐入式學步車的國家——而且是徹底地禁：進口、廣告、二手轉手、甚至拆掉輪子，全部都違法。

visual.alt: Political map of North America — base for the BANNED 2004 (Canada) / STILL SOLD (USA) contrast

scenes.beat: ACT C — why the US never banned: Shin verbatim quote on CPSC legal bar
scenes.narration: 二十年過去，美國還是沒跟上。不是因為證據比較弱——是同一台機器——而是兩國的法律寫法不同。一位消費者報告的政策顧問這樣說：virtually impossible for the CPSC to ban a consumer product. 在美國，要讓 CPSC 禁掉一項消費品並在法庭上站得住腳，幾乎不可能——除非國會直接下令。

visual.alt: Blank political map of North America — the US that never banned the walker

overlay.name: "virtually impossible for the CPSC to ban a consumer product"
overlay.role: Oriene Shin, Consumer Reports policy counsel, 2024

scenes.beat: ACT C — lobbying half + still legal and sold in 2024
scenes.narration: 另一半原因是遊說。加拿大的監管者，沒有美國這邊製造商給的政治壓力。於是美國選擇了設計標準，而不是禁令——所以這款有輪坐入式學步車，到二零二四年，在美國還是合法、還在賣。

visual.alt: Political map of North America — the US chose design standards over a ban under manufacturer lobbying pressure

overlay.text: 美國選擇設計標準，而非禁令

scenes.beat: ACT D — BMJ 2002 milestones bar chart (weeks of delay vs non-users)
scenes.narration: 醫學界還有第二個反對理由，常被安全爭論蓋過：就算它一個孩子都沒弄傷——它根本做不到盒子上暗示的那件事。一項一百九十名嬰兒的 BMJ 對照研究發現，用學步車的孩子，反而更晚達到每一個動作里程碑：爬、站、走，全部都晚了三到四週。

visual.title: 用學步車的孩子，每個里程碑都更晚
visual.background_prompt: aged paper texture, soft sepia stains, faint grid
visual.subtitle: 對照非使用者

scenes.beat: ACT D — dose-response line chart (delay days vs use hours)
scenes.narration: 而且劑量越大、延遲越久——每在座椅裡待二十四小時，走路就大約再晚三天。它替嬰兒做的那些動作，正是嬰兒需要靠自己練起來的肌肉與平衡。

visual.title: 延遲隨使用時間增加
visual.background_prompt: aged paper texture, soft sepia stains, faint grid
visual.subtitle: x: 使用時數 · y: 延遲天數

scenes.beat: ACT D — AAP verbatim line: walkers don't help and may delay motor development
scenes.narration: 兒科學會的結論很直白——do not help a child learn to walk and may delay motor development. 學步車不會幫孩子學會走路，反而可能延遲他的動作發展。

visual.alt: A child in a wheeled sit-in walker, 2022 — the device the AAP says does not help

overlay.name: "do not help a child learn to walk and may delay motor development"

scenes.beat: $1.1B market paradox as animated big number — replaces the static slide
scenes.narration: 你會以為，故事到這裡結束。但全球學步車市場現在估值十一億美元，每年還在以百分之四成長。

visual.title: 市場仍在成長
visual.background_prompt: aged paper texture, soft sepia stains, faint grid

scenes.beat: Explains market persistence through product confusion and naming chaos
scenes.narration: 為什麼？因為「學步車」這三個字，其實同時指三種完全不一樣的產品。研究者統計，它有四十多個不同的名字。

narration_alt.en: Why? Because the words baby walker actually cover three mechanically different products. Researchers have counted over 40 names for them.

scenes.beat: Proposes solution through product categorization rather than blanket judgment
scenes.narration: 所以，與其爭論該不該禁，不如先把這三種產品分清楚。它們的危險，差距非常大。

visual.text:
Three different products
share one name

narration_alt.en: So instead of debating the ban, let's separate the three products. Their risk profiles are not even close.

scenes.beat: Defines the dangerous wheeled seat walker type
scenes.narration: 第一種，有輪坐入式學步車——也就是醫師警告的那一種。寶寶用布墊吊在裡面，雙腳穿過去著地，下面四個輪子。

visual.alt: A child in a wheeled sit-in walker, 2022 — the dangerous design, still sold today

narration_alt.en: Product one: the wheeled sit-in walker. The dangerous one. The baby is suspended in a fabric seat, legs through, four wheels below.

scenes.beat: Explains the core safety problem of premature mobility
scenes.narration: 問題就在這裡：它讓還不會走的嬰兒，突然能用每秒九十公分的速度衝刺，一秒到樓梯邊。

visual.text:
Wheeled sit-in walker
3 ft / sec
faster than most adults can intercept

narration_alt.en: Here's the problem: a baby who can't walk yet can suddenly sprint at 3 feet per second — and reach a stairwell in one beat.

scenes.beat: Alerts readers that dangerous models remain legally available
scenes.narration: 重點是：這款學步車在台灣、在美國，現在還是合法銷售。嬰兒用品店裡，依舊看得到。

visual.alt: A child in a wheeled sit-in walker, 2022 — still legal, still sold

narration_alt.en: And here's the key: this product is still legal and still sold — in the US, in Taiwan, on the shelves you walk past.

scenes.beat: Introduces the safer push walker alternative
scenes.narration: 第二種，學步推車。寶寶站在後面，雙手扶著它，自己一步一步往前推。完全不一樣的東西。

visual.alt: push-toy walker

narration_alt.en: Here's the key: still legal in the US, still sold — on the shelves you walk past.

scenes.beat: Contrasts push walker mechanics with dangerous seated version
scenes.narration: 結構上正好相反：孩子是站立的，承擔自己的體重，靠自己的步伐前進。沒有懸吊座椅，也沒有突然加速的問題。

visual.title: 結構正好相反

left.label: 坐入式學步車
left.value:
孩子懸吊在座椅裡
—自己不承重

right.label: 學步推車
right.value:
孩子站立，自己承重
—練習真實肌力

visual.subtitle: 有懸吊座椅 → 突然加速 → 危險
visual.background_prompt: aged paper texture, soft sepia stains, faint grid

narration_alt.en: Mechanically, it's the inverse: the child is upright, bearing their own weight, moving at their own pace. No suspended seat, no speed problem.

scenes.beat: Provides medical endorsement of push walker benefits
scenes.narration: 兒科醫師對這款的態度是——可以。它在做的事，和孩子自然學走路是同一條路：練平衡、練步幅、練肌肉。

visual.alt: toddler using push-toy walker

narration_alt.en: Pediatricians consider these fine. What they do is what natural walking does — balance, stride, muscle memory. Useful practice, not replacement.

scenes.beat: Offers practical selection criteria for push walkers
scenes.narration: 選購重點：底盤要夠寬、不會翻；輪子最好有阻力，不要太滑；買的是站著推的，不是大孩子的滑步車。

visual.text:
Push-toy checklist
• wide base
• resistance wheels
• stand-behind, not ride-on

narration_alt.en: Shopping tips: a wide base so it won't tip, wheels with resistance not just slip, and a model the child stands behind — not a ride-on.

scenes.beat: Introduces stationary activity center as third product type
scenes.narration: 第三種，定點活動架。看起來像學步車，但沒有輪子。寶寶坐在中間的彈跳座位，旁邊一圈玩具。

visual.prompt: Studio product photograph: an empty baby stationary activity center (Exersaucer-style) standing on a clean wooden floor — NO baby visible — a round plastic activity tray ringed with built-in hanging toys, a padded rotating seat suspended in the center, sturdy splayed plastic legs resting flat on the floor with NO wheels at the base, soft natural window light from the side, warm sepia color grade, three-quarter angle at child eye level, photo-realistic, neutral home interior background
visual.alt: stationary activity center — no wheels, defining the product type

narration_alt.en: Product three: the stationary activity center. Looks like a walker, but has no wheels. Baby sits in a bouncy seat ringed with toys.

scenes.beat: Presents activity centers as medically recommended safe alternative
scenes.narration: 這就是兒科學會二零零一年公開推薦的替代品。它不會跑、不會撞下樓梯、不會把寶寶突然送到熱鍋邊。

narration_alt.en: This is the alternative the AAP explicitly endorsed in 2001. It can't run, can't fall down stairs, can't reach a stove.

scenes.beat: Warns against overuse of stationary activity centers
scenes.narration: 但要注意一個但書：太久把孩子綁在裡面，會延遲他自己練習動作的時間。短時間用是好工具，整天放就不是。

visual.text:
Stationary activity center
short sessions ✓
prolonged use ✗

narration_alt.en: One caveat: leaving a child in it too long can delay independent motor development. Short sessions are fine; a whole afternoon is not.

scenes.beat: Provides selection and usage guidelines for activity centers
scenes.narration: 選購重點：底座要穩、不會翻；座位高度可調，讓寶寶的雙腳能平踩到地板；用的時候，每次別超過一段時間。

visual.text:
Activity center checklist
• stable wide base
• adjustable seat
• limit session length

narration_alt.en: Shopping tips: stable wide base, height-adjustable seat so feet rest flat on the floor, and limit each session.

scenes.beat: Summarizes safety hierarchy of the three product types
scenes.narration: 三種產品擺在一起：危險的是有輪坐入式；安全的是學步推車；活動架沒有輪子，是另一個類別。

visual.title: 同一個名字，三種產品

left.label: 有輪坐入式 — 危險
left.value:
懸吊座椅 + 輪子
速度 + 延伸觸及 = 事故

right.label: 學步推車 — 安全
right.value:
站立自推，無座椅
練習真實步行肌力

visual.subtitle: 定點活動架 = 無輪，另一類別
visual.background_prompt: aged paper texture, soft sepia stains, faint grid

narration_alt.en: Three products side by side: the wheeled sit-in is the dangerous one. The push-toy is safe. The stationary center is a different category entirely.

scenes.beat: Distills safety rule into simple terms
scenes.narration: 規則其實非常簡單。Wheels + suspended seat = the one to avoid. 同時有輪子和吊式座椅，就是要避開的那一種；少了其中一個，就是另一個產品類別。

visual.alt: Push-toy walker — the opposite of the design to avoid

overlay.name: "Wheels + suspended seat = the one to avoid"

narration_alt.en: The rule is simple. Wheels plus a suspended seat — the one to avoid.

scenes.beat: Warns about naming confusion and emphasizes design-based evaluation
scenes.narration: 中文裡這幾個產品的名字也很亂——學步車、助行器、健力架——同樣的字常常指不同東西。買之前，先看設計，不要只看名字。

visual.alt: closing — push-toy as the safe positive close

narration_alt.en: The naming is messy in every language — researchers counted over 40 terms. Before you buy, look at the design, not the label.

title: 600 年的學步車：醫界用 40 年才終於降伏的設計
description: 從 1440 年的彩飾手抄本到今天的 11 億美元市場——學步車的安全爭議。
